title: Q2 Product Update — Town Hall Draft (notes to self)
content:
Notes to self for the Q2 all-hands product update. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of TODOs and scribbles. Keep informal.

Objective:
- Give an upbeat update that signals product momentum without overpromising availability or timelines.
- Surface 3 customer stories + 2 measurable wins (latency, cost) + one production risk and our mitigation.
- Keep the demo short (90s) and push people to the console tour microsite after the talk.

Topline messages (3):
1) Reliability: Dedicated capacity SLA rollout is on track; first 10 customers migrated and no regressions in p50/p99. highlight: "<20ms median inference for text-generation-1 in EU region for typical 1k-batch workloads" (validate numbers with infra).
2) Cost/control: Redwood Optimize beta reduced per-token spend by ~18% on average for early adopters (caveat: model mix skewed to llama-variants).
3) Consistency across modes: same API, same tooling whether hosted/dedicated/private — show one-liner code snippet as reminder.

Demo plan (90s):
- 0:00–0:10 show the simple REST call (one line) -> emphasize same call for hosted/dedicated/private
- 0:10–0:50 run the console quick-play demo (pre-recorded) showing routing policy switch (latency -> cost) and instant fallback to smaller model when capacity limited
- 0:50–1:30 show tracing + token-cost breakdown for one call and the rollback toggle (can revert model rollout)

Notes / staging checklist:
- Use pre-recorded console capture (no live infra risk). Priya to confirm console recording cleaned up by EOD 4/14.
- Verify hosted API keys used are sandbox keys (no PII).
- Ensure the trace shows realistic timestamps (not obviously simulated).

Q&A prep (anticipated questions and short answers):
Q: When will Dedicated be generally available for small customers?
A: Targeting GA in late Q3; early access for customers on reserved commit now. Avoid exact dates — say "late Q3" + point to sales channel.

Q: Any plans for new model types / multimodal?
A: Yes — roadmap includes multimodal prototype work and partnerships; no public dates yet. Point to research demos in the Confluence link.

Q: What about price cuts and rate limits?
A: We continuously tune pricing based on unit economics. Optimize suggestions have led to 18% improvements for betas; we'll expand coverage in Q3. Rate limits remain per-plan and we will publish clearer guardrails in the docs.

Risk slide (must mention, keep concise):
- Risk: Early quantization on some popular models introduced subtle output drift for high-precision tasks (e.g., code generation).
- Mitigation: we added targeted quality gates (prompt-based evals) and automatic rollback for canary traffic; pausing aggressive quantization for models used heavily in codegen workflows.
- Ask to engineering: continue to add model-specific eval suites (Priya / Liu follow-up).

Stakeholder cues / who to cc in post-comm:
- Ops: Alex Friedman (verify metrics), Jenn H (incidents), SRE on call (monitor rollback triggers)
- Sales/CS: Maria (customer list for Dedicated invites)
- Legal: Sam (any language on compliance for private deployments)

Tone guide for delivery:
- Keep it product-first, engineering-respectful. Avoid marketing hyperbole. Use concrete numbers or cite edge cases. If metric uncertain, say "preliminary" or "early adopters".

Speaker notes (for me):
- Start: quick thank-you. 10–15s: "small set of measurable wins and a clear list of next steps for Q3". 
- Use anecdote: "We had a startup move from research to production in 6 weeks using dedicated pools — they cut tail latency in half." (confirm with SE — placeholder)
- End CTA: visit "console.redwood.ai/tour/q2" (placeholder microsite) + drop in #town-hall thread for questions.

Rehearsal checklist (TODAY):
- 1) Run through script with Priya (timing) — 30m window tomorrow 10am PT.
- 2) Finalize demo video and upload to CDN — infra to confirm link.
- 3) Confirm the numbers (latency / cost) with Alex by EOD 4/15.
- 4) Upload final slide deck to shared drive and link in the invite.

Misc scratchpad / things to consider (note-y):
- Could mention "intelligent batching" wins with a simple stat: ~22% fewer tokens processed at peak for one customer. Put a question mark, need to verify.
- Consider dropping a short FAQ doc in #all-hands after the event for questions we can't answer live. Liu to draft.
- Keep private deployment language cautious: emphasize "customer-managed networking" and no centralized data ingestion. Legal to review snippet: "We do not retain customer payloads for private deployments."

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Is the Dedicated SLA wording finalized in the recruiting doc? (Legal / Product ops)
- Which 3 customer stories do we want featured (ask CS)?

To-dos appended to this doc: (quick)
- [ ] Priya: finalize demo video link
- [ ] Alex: confirm latency / p99 numbers
- [ ] Liu: draft post-hall FAQ doc
- [ ] Maria: confirm customer names we can call out

Rough timeline for next 48 hours:
- Fri 4/11: lock slides and script
- Mon 4/14: dry run w/ Priya + SRE (30m)
- Tue 4/15: final numbers & prep published to internal site

Random notes to self (do not include in final slides):
- Keep joke about coffee consumption short. Not necessary.
- If someone asks about model interpretability, point to research blog and say we are investing in more tooling for model introspection.

End of scratchpad — convert to cleaned draft for comms team after final rehearsal.
